questions.questionText: Which statement correctly distinguishes a minimum spanning tree from other spanning trees of the same weighted graph?
options: It has the smallest possible total edge weight among all spanning trees.
It contains the maximum number of edges possible.
It always includes the heaviest edge in the graph.
It must have exactly n edges where n is the number of vertices.
questions.correctAnswer: It has the smallest possible total edge weight among all spanning trees.
questions.explanation: A minimum spanning tree (MST) is defined as the spanning tree whose sum of edge weights is minimum among all spanning trees of the graph. The other options describe incorrect properties: a spanning tree always has n‑1 edges, not n; it does not aim to maximize edges or include the heaviest edge.
